rules.when: The task is technical product design, architecture, or planning, or new feature development with no PRD and no written plan. Do not dispatch until the captain approves on the issue.
rules.why: Strongest model in the factory for open-ended design.

rules.when: The task touches auth, permissions, money, data migrations, or anything security-sensitive. Label the issue ready-for-human as well: a human must sign off before merge.
The task implements an already-specified feature: an issue with acceptance criteria, an existing PR, or a written plan.
rules.why: Workhorse: spec exists, so the mid-tier model does the build.

rules.when: The task is small and well-defined: a simple bug fix, copy or i18n change, or a docs-only change.
rules.why: Small tasks go to the cheapest, fastest model; Sonnet takes over if Haiku gets stuck.

rules.when: The task is the daily verification-skill maintenance pass.
rules.why: Multi-step pass across every feature; too broad for Haiku.

review.when: Every factory PR. Pick the first model in this list that differs from the model that authored the PR's latest commits.
review.why: Cross-model review inside the Claude family. Sonnet and Haiku work is reviewed by Opus; Opus work by Sonnet.
